INPUT FILE: [TASK]/workspace/layered/layer0/main/main.c
INLINE REFERENCE (read-only, same semantics, for understanding behavior): [TASK]/workspace/layered/layer0/main/main.inline.c
OUTPUT DIR: [TASK]/workspace/output/main/

The target function is main (the code after "/* === Target: main === */"). The headers/typedefs before it are compile setup; leave them unchanged.

Environment prefix (use this exact python for all spectool calls):
'/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python' -m engine.harness_spectool

Program summary: a stack VLA `int a[N]` with N=100000. First loop (i from 0 .. N-1): sets x=unknown(); if(x) break; a[i]=j; j=j+i; starting with j=0. So for every written index m, a[m]=sum(0..m-1)=m*(m-1)/2 >= 0. Second loop: for k=1..i-1, asserts a[k]>=0. You must prove that assertion.

Required ACSL (you should produce essentially this):
- Function `main` is a root function; a full function contract is OPTIONAL. Focus on loop annotations.
- First loop: loop invariant 0 <= i <= N; loop invariant 0 <= j; loop invariant \forall integer m; 0 <= m < i ==> a[m] >= 0; loop assigns i, j, x, a[0 .. N-1]; loop variant N - i;
- Second loop: loop invariant 1 <= k <= i; loop invariant \forall integer m; 0 <= m < i ==> a[m] >= 0; loop assigns k; loop variant i - k;
These should allow WP to prove `assert(a[k]>=0)` via the second invariant (since 1<=k<i in the body, so 0<=k<i).

Workflow:
1. Read the input file and inline reference.
2. Use the spectool `inject` command to inject the loop annotations into the input file, outputting to OUTPUT_DIR/main/main.acsl.c. loops JSON format: [{"line": 28, "acsl": "..."}, {"line": 34, "acsl": "..."}] where line is the `for` keyword line in the .c file. REMEMBER: all original C tokens MUST be preserved unchanged, and the original `//@ assert(a[k]>=0);` must remain exactly as-is. Only ADD ACSL annotations. Do NOT add any admit/assume/axiom.
   Exact inject command form: <PREFIX> inject --src <input.c> --out <OUTPUT_DIR>/main/main.acsl.c --loops '<JSON>'
3. Read the injected .acsl.c and confirm original tokens/assert preserved and annotation placement is correct (annotations immediately before the `for`).
4. Verify: <PREFIX> verify -f <OUTPUT_DIR>/main/main.acsl.c --timeout 30 --save-stdout <OUTPUT_DIR>/main/main.wp.txt
   It returns {"result": "Pass", "proved": N, "total": N, ...}. A result "Pass" requires proved == total.
5. If it fails, run <PREFIX> locate-fail --wp <OUTPUT_DIR>/main/main.wp.txt --src <OUTPUT_DIR>/main/main.acsl.c and adjust the invariants, re-inject, re-verify. Up to 5 fix rounds.
6. Work located under the given OUTPUT_DIR only. Do not read any files outside the workspace given above. Do not run help/version/config commands.

Report back (as your final text result) a JSON object:
{"status": "pass" or "fail", "proved": N, "total": N, "round": R, "error": null-or-string}
Only mark status "pass" when proved == total. Also mention the final proved/total numbers.
